layers.root: Reserved for agentic-stack, the root contract every other skill assumes. It is the seventh layer in schemas/skill.schema.json and tools/validate_skills.py, it is not listed as a skill here, and it is exempt from the used_by symmetry check by design (ceremony 1 findings C1-004 and C1-001).
layers.core: The five owned components of PASS.md B2, Document, Planner, Graph, Judge and Ledger, each importing capability interfaces only and naming no product.
layers.cap: One skill per capability interface in PASS.md B3: it names the governing standard and version, defines the contract the core imports, ships two adapters whose execution models differ, and carries the caller's view itself - the -use facet was folded into the ideal on 2026-09-03. cap-consumption is the one cross-capability member of this layer: the consumption contract every capability shares, stated once.
layers.xc: One skill per cross-cutting concern in PASS.md B4, seven in total rather than grouped, because each has a distinct enforcement point, a distinct check, and a distinct way to fail open; the matching cap- skill defines the interface while the xc- skill defines the placement that a caller cannot decline, and merging the two is what produced conformance checks that exist outside the enforcement path (claimed, per PASS.md A6).
layers.seam: The two boundaries with no standard to adopt, Dispatch and State, where original design effort is warranted and where the platform's weight sits. seam-entry-envelope and seam-agent-ingress were dropped on 2026-09-03 and folded into cap-work-intake and cap-capability-registry, restoring this definition.
layers.compose: Assemblies of lower layers into a workflow, a bounded loop, a parked approval and an agent; a composition introduces no new interface. compose-workflow was merged into compose-operators on 2026-09-03, so the closed operator set is defined once and the sequence operator is a section of it.
layers.build: The disciplines every author in this repo uses regardless of layer: definition of done with a breakage, adapter pairing, evidence recording that keeps claimed and measured apart, and the skill authoring convention.

skills.name: build-definition-of-done
skills.purpose: Make every piece of work carry a criterion, a breakage that makes the criterion fail, and the measured output of both.
skills.notes_for_author: Assert on a non-zero count of things actually checked, never on an exit code alone. PASS.md A7 finding 2 is a pipeline that was structurally green with every behavioural stage skipped (measured, per PASS.md A7). Fold-in (research gap effective-configuration-attestation-at-s, X-cross-structure-023, X-cross-structure-050, X-cross-structure-053, T-t2-03, PASS.md A7): a gate reports which stages were applicable, so a run with zero applicable behavioural stages is inconclusive rather than green; and each adapter emits at start-up the configuration it actually resolved, not the file it was given, as an attested record (in-toto/DSSE) that a validator compares against the declared configuration.

skills.name: build-adapter-pair
skills.purpose: Choose a second adapter that breaks a different assumption than the first, and record how the two execution models differ.
skills.notes_for_author: A different vendor of the same shape proves nothing. The differs-in-execution-model field is mandatory and empty means the pair is rejected. See decomposition.md section 4.

skills.name: build-evidence-record
skills.purpose: Record what was actually run, so a claim is never laundered into a measurement.
skills.notes_for_author: Fields follow the evidence records already in use: script SHA-256, git commit, tree hash under test, dirty flag (claimed, per PASS.md A5). Add the claimed-or-measured label. A result from a dirty tree may never be labelled measured.

skills.name: build-skill-authoring
skills.purpose: Fix the shape of a skill in this repo: layer prefix, Composes with section, and a cited standard with a version or the literal phrase version unverified.
skills.notes_for_author: Never invent a version number. If you are unsure, write version unverified. Products appear only in adapter fields and Part A quotations.

skills.name: cap-errors
skills.purpose: Give every failure in the platform one machine-readable shape so no caller ever parses prose.
skills.standard: RFC 9457 Problem Details for HTTP APIs
skills.adapter_today: in-process problem-details library
skills.second_adapter: gateway filter mapping upstream failures into application/problem+json without touching the service
skills.notes_for_author: The type registry in decomposition.md section 2.1.6 is closed. Extending it means adding a row there first. Typed errors are absent today (claimed, per PASS.md A6), so this skill starts from nothing rather than migrating something. Fold-in (research gap a-registered-problem-type-namespace-with, X-cross-structure-039 and X-cross-structure-040, T-t2-02, PASS.md B5): register the platform's own problem-type namespace with a minimum set of type URIs, policy-denied, budget-exceeded, idempotency-conflict, cancelled, timeout, partial-result, adapter-unavailable and schema-invalid, each with typed extension members, and make every seam return application/problem+json on failure, including the answer to what a Dispatch failure returns.

skills.name: cap-document-validation
skills.purpose: Validate any declared shape against a published schema dialect, with a validator that passes the official test suite.
skills.standard: JSON Schema 2020-12
skills.adapter_today: Python jsonschema validator
skills.second_adapter: compiled-schema validator in a different language runtime, for example a Rust or Go 2020-12 implementation
skills.notes_for_author: Does not build on cap-errors: JSON Schema 2020-12 defines its own output formats, and mapping those into problem details is the consumer's job. Keeping that separation is what lets the validator be swapped for one in another language runtime.

skills.name: cap-isolation
skills.purpose: Run a unit of work with declared resources and declared egress, so that what runs inside is opaque to how it is contained.
skills.standard: OCI Runtime Spec v1.2 or later; search indicates v1.3.0 is current (version unverified)
skills.adapter_today: Firecracker microVM
skills.second_adapter: WebAssembly component sandbox run through an OCI-conformant shim
skills.notes_for_author: Express declared resources and declared egress, never a machine configuration. Any field only a virtual machine can honour is a leak. Egress defaults off and no real secret enters the unit (claimed, per PASS.md A3). Whether the second adapter can claim full OCI conformance is open question 5.

skills.name: cap-model-access
skills.purpose: Obtain a completion from a class of model without naming a vendor, and without the caller knowing whether the call is synchronous.
skills.standard: OpenAI-compatible chat completions, de facto, no ratified specification (version unverified)
skills.adapter_today: OpenAI-compatible gateway (LiteLLM)
skills.second_adapter: provider-native asynchronous batch submission with claim-and-poll
skills.notes_for_author: Model a completion as a future with a claim ticket, so synchronous and batch are one interface. Callers request a class, never a vendor (claimed, per PASS.md A4). The OpenAI-shaped batch route already failed once by branching on three provider names (claimed, per PASS.md A4); do not reproduce that shape. Fold-in (research gap routing-policy-a-pure-function-from-clas, X-end-to-end-056, X-end-to-end-057, X-end-to-end-058, T-t2-02, PASS.md B3): route with a pure function from (class, unit of work, budget remaining, policy verdict) to an endpoint selection, evaluated before the adapter is called, so routing is testable without a model. The adapter contrast to record is gateway-side group routing versus a semantic router that composes routing with policy and reasoning budget, the second breaking the assumption that the class is decided by the caller's prefix.

skills.name: cap-durable-execution
skills.purpose: Let a multi-step unit of work survive a crash and resume at the first incomplete step.
skills.standard: none published; see decomposition.md section 2 (searched, none found)
skills.adapter_today: external workflow orchestrator with deterministic replay (Temporal)
skills.second_adapter: in-process transactional step log over a relational database
skills.notes_for_author: No published standard exists; search query 8 in decomposition.md found none (claimed). Express step, key, checkpoint, resume point and nothing more. Anything that only makes sense under deterministic replay is an orchestrator detail. The orchestrator is present but not listening today (claimed, per PASS.md A6), which is the reason the interface must not assume a server.

skills.name: cap-agent-runtime
skills.purpose: Drive an agent through one prompt turn and learn why the turn stopped.
skills.standard: Agent Client Protocol (protocol version unverified; TypeScript SDK v0.21.1 seen in search results)
skills.adapter_today: ACP agent over JSON-RPC on stdio (goose)
skills.second_adapter: single-shot non-interactive agent with no client callbacks
skills.notes_for_author: The unit is a prompt turn with a stop reason. Everything interactive, including permission callbacks and streaming, is negotiated at session start and optional. Cancel mid-tool-call ends the turn in about 8 seconds against a 45 second operation with zero trailing frames (measured, per PASS.md A3); that number is where the 10 second default grace window came from.

skills.name: cap-tool-access
skills.purpose: Let a unit of work reach tools published by anyone, over a protocol no caller needs our library to speak.
skills.standard: Model Context Protocol, specification revision 2026-07-28 (claimed)
skills.adapter_today: in-house MCP endpoint
skills.second_adapter: any third-party MCP server reached over the same client
skills.notes_for_author: The criterion must assert a non-zero tool count as well as conformance. An endpoint that is live, authenticated and has zero tools registered passes conformance and does nothing (claimed, per PASS.md A6).

skills.name: cap-capability-packaging
skills.purpose: Package a capability so a conformant runtime we did not write can load it.
skills.standard: Agent Skills spec, published as an open standard (version unverified)
skills.adapter_today: filesystem skill directories
skills.second_adapter: registry-served skill packages distributed as OCI artifacts
skills.notes_for_author: The spec requires only name and description in frontmatter (claimed). This repo adds the Composes with link check on top; keep the two separable so the packaging check stays spec-conformant rather than repo-specific. Fold-in (research gap uniform-packaging-for-every-composable-u, X-entry-composition-035, X-entry-composition-036, X-entry-composition-056, T-t2-01, PASS.md B3): one packaging shape for every composable unit, name and description resident, body on trigger, references on use, with the tier budgets as the machine-checkable simplicity test (build-simplicity-budget) and publication to a registry rather than copying between projects (cap-capability-registry).

skills.name: cap-work-intake
skills.purpose: Accept a job from any producer and turn it into one canonical document, whatever the producer was.
skills.standard: CloudEvents v1.0.2 (version unverified) and A2A protocol v1.0 (version unverified; specification text could not be fetched, domain egress-blocked)
skills.adapter_today: CloudEvents over HTTP from CLI, git events and schedules
skills.second_adapter: A2A message producer mapped into the canonical envelope
skills.notes_for_author: Idempotency and scheduling are apparent dependencies, not real ones: a schedule is one producer among several and the replay lease is applied above by xc-idempotency-lease. Whether both envelope formats stay first-class is open question 10. Fold-in (consolidation part A, 2026-09-03; kb/ceremonies/consolidation-review.json plan steps 7 and 8): the planned skill seam-entry-envelope and its -implement facet were dropped and their content belongs here. Its purpose was: Make every driving adapter produce one identical internal record, so nothing downstream ever branches on how the work arrived. Capability: Entry envelope. Standard: CloudEvents v1.0.2 core context attributes and HTTP protocol binding (version unverified). Adapter today: an HTTP driving adapter accepting a CloudEvent, plus the CLI adapter, both emitting the same envelope. Second adapter: a git-event or schedule adapter where no caller supplies ids, deriving the idempotency key as a fingerprint of selected payload elements, which breaks the assumption that the producer supplies the correlation and idempotency fields. Its definition of done: Identical work submitted through every entry adapter produces byte-identical envelopes apart from the source attribute and the minted run id, and an adapter that omits actor, ceiling or idempotency key is refused at the boundary instead of defaulted. Its notes were: Cite X-entry-composition-001, X-entry-composition-003, X-entry-composition-004, X-entry-composition-005 and X-entry-composition-015 for the envelope, X-cross-structure-016, X-cross-structure-017, X-cross-structure-018 and X-cross-structure-019 for the normalising mapping; target requirement T-t2-03; PASS.md B3. The envelope carries the CloudEvents required context attributes (id, source, specversion, type) plus actor and delegation chain, the correlation envelope, the budget ceiling and the idempotency key; every routing decision and every cross-cutting concern reads only this record. The platform mints its own run id and preserves the source protocol's ids as attributes rather than replacing them, so a caller can still find its own work. This is a seam and not a capability because no standard covers the mapping, only the envelope shape. Schedules and manual triggers are sibling entries producing this same envelope (folded into cap-scheduling), and the Document every adapter produces is core-document. Closes raw gaps entry-envelope-one-internal-record-every and an-intake-normaliser-one-required-mappin.

skills.name: cap-telemetry
skills.purpose: Emit traces and metrics in a form any collector can ingest, with correlation carried explicitly.
skills.standard: OTLP (version unverified) and OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions (pre-stable; version unverified)
skills.adapter_today: OTLP SDK exporting to a trace UI and ingestion API (Langfuse)
skills.second_adapter: plain OTLP collector writing to a columnar store with no LLM-specific interface
skills.notes_for_author: Do not build on trace parentage. W3C trace context does not survive the agent boundary; a depth-3 task tree produces three unrelated root traces (measured, per PASS.md A7 finding 1). GenAI semantic conventions are pre-stable with every attribute at Development stability as of mid-2026 (claimed), so cite them as unstable. Fold-in (research gaps split-the-telemetry-interface-a-stable-t and pin-the-genai-convention-version-in-the; X-cross-structure-009, X-cross-structure-010, X-cross-structure-011, X-entry-composition-050, X-entry-composition-051, X-entry-composition-015; T-t2-02 and T-t2-03; PASS.md B3 and B4): split the interface in two, a stable transport and shape contract pinned to OTLP 1.11.0 and a separately versioned attribute mapping for the experimental GenAI conventions that can be revised without touching emitters, and record the semconv version each run emitted against. Keep the platform's own correlation fields (xc-correlation-envelope) independent of that mapping, so a convention revision changes one adapter and not the entry envelope. build-interface-versioning is the general discipline this instantiates.

skills.name: cap-policy
skills.purpose: Get a deterministic allow-or-deny decision, with the rule that decided it, from a policy engine.
skills.standard: Rego policy language with a decision API; no ratified standard (version unverified)
skills.adapter_today: Open Policy Agent
skills.second_adapter: Cedar policy engine behind the same decision API
skills.notes_for_author: This skill defines the decision API only. Where the decision is consulted belongs to xc-policy-gate. Conformance checks exist today and are not wired into the enforcement path (claimed, per PASS.md A6); that is what happens when the two are treated as one thing.

skills.name: cap-provenance
skills.purpose: Produce a signed statement about an artifact that a tool we did not write can verify.
skills.standard: in-toto Attestation Framework v1 (version unverified), DSSE (version unverified), SLSA v1.0 (v1.1 unverified)
skills.adapter_today: append-only JSONL evidence records wrapped in DSSE envelopes
skills.second_adapter: keyless signing with a public transparency log (Sigstore)
skills.notes_for_author: The criterion must run an external verifier, not ours. If verification needs our store, the requirement in PASS.md B4 is not met. Evidence records and attestations are different things: build-evidence-record is note-taking, this is a signed envelope. Fold-in (research gap two-provenance-predicates-behind-one-att, X-cross-structure-050, X-cross-structure-051, X-cross-structure-054, T-t2-02, PASS.md B4): two predicates behind one capability, a build-shaped predicate for artifacts (SLSA provenance) and a run-shaped predicate for agent actions (actor, tool, argument digest, result digest, decision refs), both emitted as in-toto Statements in DSSE envelopes so one verifier handles both. There is no standard predicate for agent actions, so mark that half proposed.

skills.name: cap-identity
skills.purpose: Name the actor behind every action, including delegated agent actors, with an explicit chain.
skills.standard: OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange RFC 8693, plus workload identity
skills.adapter_today: OIDC provider issuing exchanged tokens
skills.second_adapter: SPIFFE/SPIRE workload attestation issuing X.509-SVIDs
skills.notes_for_author: There is no identity field anywhere in the system today (claimed, per PASS.md A6), so this starts from nothing rather than migrating something, and the P13 check starts red by construction. Do not build on the policy engine; policy consumes identity, not the reverse. Fold-in (research gap actor-binding-at-entry-each-driving-adap is placed in xc-identity-delegation; the dropped gap an-identity-capability-with-two-operatio duplicated this skill, X-cross-structure-034 through X-cross-structure-038, T-t2-03): state the two operations explicitly, attest (issue an SVID to a unit, including by a delegated path for workloads the platform cannot attest in place) and delegate (exchange a subject token plus an actor token for a scoped token whose act claim names the acting agent, nested to express a chain). Authorisation reads only the current actor; the chain is recorded in provenance.

skills.name: cap-scheduling
skills.purpose: Compute when a recurring unit of work is due, as a pure function of a rule and a window.
skills.standard: RFC 5545 recurrence rules
skills.adapter_today: orchestrator-native schedules
skills.second_adapter: standalone RFC 5545 evaluator driving a queue
skills.notes_for_author: Test vectors must include both DST boundaries, a leap day and a BYSETPOS rule, because a fixed-interval cron passes everything else. Do not source recurrence from an orchestrator's scheduler; that makes the orchestrator unswappable for a reason unrelated to orchestration. Fold-in (research gap schedules-and-manual-triggers-declared-a, X-entry-composition-049, X-entry-composition-044, X-entry-composition-045, X-entry-composition-001, T-t1-03, PASS.md B3): a schedule and a manual trigger are sibling entries declared on the same unit, the schedule as a single portable RFC 5545 recurrence string and the trigger as a typed input schema the surface renders, and both produce the standard entry envelope (seam-entry-envelope) rather than a private path into the platform.

skills.name: cap-idempotency
skills.purpose: Make a repeated external request produce one execution and one answer.
skills.standard: Idempotency-Key HTTP header field, draft-ietf-httpapi-idempotency-key-header-07, expired, never an RFC (claimed)
skills.adapter_today: idempotency key carried on the wire with no lease
skills.second_adapter: conditional-write lease store on a transactional database
skills.notes_for_author: The header convention expired without becoming an RFC (claimed), so adopt the field name and specify the lease semantics ourselves in decomposition.md section 2.1.6. Today the key is on the wire with no lease (claimed, per PASS.md B3); the key alone deduplicates nothing. Fold-in (research gap idempotency-capability-claim-key-payload, X-cross-structure-041, X-cross-structure-042, X-cross-structure-043, T-t2-03, PASS.md B4): the operation is claim(key, payload_digest) returning fresh, duplicate(result_ref) or conflict, applied at every entry point and at each recorded step boundary. Conflict, meaning the same key with a different payload, must return a typed error, per the draft's MUST.

skills.name: cap-state-persistence
skills.purpose: Put an opaque record somewhere durable, get it back, and prove nobody changed it.
skills.standard: none published for the store; RFC 9162 for integrity, RFC 8785 for canonical bytes
skills.adapter_today: hash-chained append-only line-delimited JSON
skills.second_adapter: content-addressed Merkle log with inclusion and consistency proofs over an object store
skills.notes_for_author: Defined over opaque records. This interface must not know that a record is a graph edge or a ledger entry; that is seam-state's job. Express integrity as give me a proof about this record at this head, never as rehash the whole log, or the object-store adapter is unimplementable.

skills.name: core-document
skills.purpose: Declare intent, a definition of done and steps as validated data, before anything reads it.
skills.notes_for_author: Core skill: no product name may appear. The document is written before any consumer exists, and it must be, because a planner that shapes the document has made planning impure. The definition of done lives here; the criterion text does not travel to the graded unit (see core-judge). Fold-in (research gaps one-document-schema-that-every-entry-ada and executable-acceptance-criteria-the-docum; X-entry-composition-052, X-entry-composition-005, X-entry-composition-026, X-end-to-end-076, X-end-to-end-077, X-end-to-end-078; T-t3-01 and T-t4-03; PASS.md B2): one schema that every entry adapter produces, carrying the composition operators of compose-operators as its step vocabulary, so a human, an agent and an event all yield the same reviewable, diffable, replayable artifact; and a definition of done that is a list of runnable checks with declared risk tiers, where a run in which no behavioural check executed is reported inconclusive, never passed. The ideal facet also carries the usability section (how a human, an agent, and an event reach it; minimal inputs/outputs; failure shape) since this layer has no separate -use skill.

skills.name: core-graph
skills.purpose: Compose typed nodes and typed existence, interface and implementation edges, with validity decidable in memory.
skills.notes_for_author: Core skill: zero outward dependencies, no product names. Persistence is a separate seam. If this skill acquires a storage engine's shape, the boundary has been drawn wrong. The ideal facet also carries the usability section (how a human, an agent, and an event reach it; minimal inputs/outputs; failure shape) since this layer has no separate -use skill.

skills.name: core-judge
skills.purpose: Turn a result and a hidden criterion into a verdict, as a pure function.
skills.notes_for_author: Design rule 6 is the whole point: the criterion never appears in anything the graded unit can read. The C4 check greps recorded dispatch requests for the criterion string and expects zero matches. Whether the judge runs inside or outside isolation is open question 6; the default is outside. Fold-in (research gap judge-extension-criterion-sampling-drop, X-end-to-end-012 and X-end-to-end-013, T-t4-04, PASS.md B2): hiding the criterion is necessary but not sufficient, because a fixed rubric leaks through outcomes over repeated runs. Add criterion sampling (drop a random subset per grading) and a periodic held-out gold-judge audit whose divergence from the routine judge is an alarm, not a score. The adapter contrast to record is a model-graded judge versus a purely deterministic verifier over the same criterion set. The ideal facet also carries the usability section (how a human, an agent, and an event reach it; minimal inputs/outputs; failure shape) since this layer has no separate -use skill.

skills.name: core-ledger
skills.purpose: Keep an append-only record across runs and be the single authority on whether work was already done.
skills.notes_for_author: Append-only means a duplicate key never overwrites. The dedup query is what stops a planner re-planning finished work, so it is part of the state query surface in decomposition.md section 2.2.5. The ideal facet also carries the usability section (how a human, an agent, and an event reach it; minimal inputs/outputs; failure shape) since this layer has no separate -use skill.

skills.name: xc-typed-errors
skills.purpose: Enforce that no failure anywhere is discovered by matching strings.
skills.notes_for_author: The check is a grep over the tree outside the problem-details parser. An adapter whose untyped-failure count is non-zero is not conformant; do not let it be waved through as a known gap. Fold-in (research gap one-problem-detail-type-registry-used-by, X-entry-composition-046 and X-entry-composition-042, T-t2-03, PASS.md B3): every driving adapter reads one shared problem-detail type registry, so a policy refusal, a budget termination and a validation failure carry the same machine-readable type whichever way the caller entered. The ideal facet also carries the usability section (how a human, an agent, and an event reach it; minimal inputs/outputs; failure shape) since this layer has no separate -use skill.

skills.name: xc-correlation
skills.purpose: Enforce that every emitted signal carries the explicit run and root dispatch identifiers.
skills.notes_for_author: This exists because injecting TRACEPARENT does not work: the agent mints its own root trace and a depth-3 tree yields three unrelated roots (measured, per PASS.md A7 finding 1). Permit more than one trace id; do not permit a missing run identifier. Resource attribute versus span attribute is open question 8. The ideal facet also carries the usability section (how a human, an agent, and an event reach it; minimal inputs/outputs; failure shape) since this layer has no separate -use skill. Fold-in (consolidation part A, 2026-09-03; kb/ceremonies/consolidation-review.json plan steps 7 and 8): the planned skill xc-correlation-envelope and its -implement facet were dropped and their content belongs here. Its purpose was: Fix the named, versioned field set that says which run a signal belongs to, and the carrier it rides on at each boundary. Its definition of done: A depth-3 task tree entered through each of the three entry points yields one run id across all three subtrees, and a boundary that drops one field of the envelope fails the check rather than degrading quietly. Its notes were: Cite X-cross-structure-004, X-cross-structure-005, X-cross-structure-007, X-cross-structure-008, X-cross-structure-012, X-cross-structure-013 and X-cross-structure-016; target requirement T-t2-03; PASS.md B4 and A7 finding 1. Fields: run id, parent unit id, entry-point kind, conversation id, idempotency key, budget ceiling id, actor chain ref. Carriers, one per boundary: OTel resource attribute in-process, W3C Baggage in-flight (bounded to 64 entries and 8192 bytes, and it leaks across boundaries), a CloudEvents Distributed Tracing extension attribute over events, and a dispatch request field over the VM boundary. Use gen_ai.conversation.id where a conversation exists; there is no standard attribute for a multi-agent session id (semantic-conventions-genai issue #51 is open), so mark that field ours. xc-correlation states the rule that correlation is explicit rather than inherited from trace parentage; this fixes the fields and the carriers so a new boundary has nothing left to invent. Closes raw gap correlation-envelope-a-named-versioned-s.

skills.name: xc-identity-delegation
skills.purpose: Enforce that every action names an actor and every delegated action carries an explicit, acyclic chain.
skills.notes_for_author: Delegation chains are ordered oldest hop first and must terminate at a root workload identity. The chain is data carried by dispatch; dispatch does not define it. Fold-in (research gap actor-binding-at-entry-each-driving-adap, X-entry-composition-048, X-entry-composition-042, X-entry-composition-015, T-t2-03, PASS.md B4): the binding point is entry. Each driving adapter attaches the actor and, where the caller acts for someone, the delegation chain onto the entry envelope (seam-entry-envelope) before any planning or spend, so no later stage has to reconstruct who asked. The ideal facet also carries the usability section (how a human, an agent, and an event reach it; minimal inputs/outputs; failure shape) since this layer has no separate -use skill.

skills.name: xc-policy-gate
skills.purpose: Enforce that refusal is deterministic and happens before any metered call.
skills.notes_for_author: The check is a timestamp ordering assertion with zero inversions plus a spend delta of exactly zero on a denied dispatch. Consulting policy in parallel with the first call fails it, which is the failure this skill exists to prevent. The ideal facet also carries the usability section (how a human, an agent, and an event reach it; minimal inputs/outputs; failure shape) since this layer has no separate -use skill.

skills.name: xc-provenance-chain
skills.purpose: Enforce that every artifact has an attestation whose subject digest matches it.
skills.notes_for_author: Orphan artifacts, meaning an output digest with no attestation, are the failure mode. Chaining attestations to a sealed log head belongs to seam-state; producing and signing them belongs here. The ideal facet also carries the usability section (how a human, an agent, and an event reach it; minimal inputs/outputs; failure shape) since this layer has no separate -use skill.

skills.name: xc-budget
skills.purpose: Enforce a spend ceiling on every unit of work, outside the unit, terminating the unit and not the platform.
skills.notes_for_author: A unit that enforces its own ceiling can decline to. Scoped keys already terminate spend rather than record it (measured, per PASS.md A4), so match that model. on_exceed is a const in the request schema, not an enum: there is no opt-out to express. Granularity is open question 7. Fold-in (research gap run-scoped-budget-one-ceiling-per-root-u, X-end-to-end-045 through X-end-to-end-048, T-t2-03, PASS.md B4): one ceiling per root unit of work, decremented by every descendant, enforced mid-run with continue, narrow, require-approval or stop, plus explicit delegation depth and fan-out caps. FOCUS v1.3 (split cost allocation) is the schema for the cost record. The adapter contrast to record is gateway virtual-key caps versus a platform-held budget lease decremented before each dispatch, the second breaking the assumption that the model gateway is the only place spend occurs. The ideal facet also carries the usability section (how a human, an agent, and an event reach it; minimal inputs/outputs; failure shape) since this layer has no separate -use skill.

skills.name: xc-idempotency-lease
